answer: A reputation system can require an agent to post a bond before it may influence a market, then slash that bond when a challenge proves its identity is duplicative or its claims are fabricated. A thread of signed interactions links the agent’s history to the bond, while a whisper of cheap new accounts cannot buy influence without fresh capital. The inlet is open to newcomers, but each identity must put scarce funds at risk, making mass Sybil creation costly rather than impossible.
